# On-page wording for compliance review

72 Street (SEBI RA INH000029722). The site gives readings on every stock. None may read as a recommendation. These are the phrases that carry the most risk, for sign-off or rewording.

Every page carries: "What the data shows, not a recommendation to buy or sell." The footer carries the registration line and the risk statement.

## 1. Stock or Index page: verdict headline, generated by rule for each name

Built as "[price phrase], and [positioning phrase]".

| Price phrase | Rule |
|---|---|
| Options are expensive | IV above 70% of recent sessions, and at least 3 points above actual moves |
| Option prices are high, matching the moves | IV above 70% of recent sessions, close to actual moves |
| Options are fairly priced | Everything else |
| Option prices are low, matching the moves | IV below 30% of recent sessions, close to actual moves |
| Options are cheap | IV below 30% of recent sessions, and at least 3 points below actual moves |

| Positioning phrase | Rule |
|---|---|
| call writing stands out | Fresh call OI against put OI in the top 15% of F&O stocks that day |
| put writing stands out | The bottom 15% |
| positions are balanced | Everything else |

Also shown: "A close above X would mean call writers have lost that level." and the same for puts.

**Questions:** does "expensive" or "cheap" imply a trade? Is "What would change this" acceptable?

## 2. Stocks in focus (Today): six stocks a day

Tags: "Signals up", "Signals down", "Mixed". Example titles: "Strong results, market agreed", "Good numbers, sold anyway", "Fresh shorts in futures", "New buying in futures".

**This is the highest risk on the site.** "Signals up" against a named stock is the closest thing we have to a directional view. Please decide whether the tag stays, and whether the 30-day blackout could apply.

## 3. Track record

Focus readings are scored as "right" or "wrong" after 5 and 20 sessions against an index of stocks their size (Nifty 100, Midcap 150, Smallcap 250). The headline is the gap between signals-up and signals-down readings, in percentage points, with a plain note on whether it could be chance and the coin-toss range for the hit rate. Nothing is shown until 30 different stocks and 20 sessions are checked. Repeats of the same call within 5 sessions count once; readings logged after 9 pm and mixed readings are shown but not counted. Past performance rules need checking here.

## 4. Live F&O

Long buildup, Short buildup, Short covering, Long unwinding. "OI up with price up is fresh buying. OI up with price down is fresh selling." "One-way moves up", "One-way moves down".

## 5. Stock page

One-line summary, for example "Strong results (profit +34%), but the trend is down and it is near its 52 week low." Chart strength bands: Strong, Constructive, Neutral, Weak, Broken. Desk calls appear only when an analyst publishes one under the call policy.

## 6. Market mood (Today)

Bumper Tezi, Tezi, "Tezi, sambhal ke", "Bazaar so raha hai", "Na tezi, na mandi", Bikwali, Mandi, Bhaari Mandi. Lines such as "Selling is broad and fear is rising." These describe the whole market, never a stock. Also "Aapke jaane ke baad" on the since-your-last-visit strip.

## 7. Data and method notes on the page

"IV and Greeks are calculated by 72 Street", "Priced range is what option prices imply by expiry. It is not a forecast." Data sources are named in the footer. Licensing of NSE, Yahoo and Screener data is a separate open question.


## Price Structure (added 11 Nov 2026)

Pages: the Structure switch on every stock chart, the Price structure card, and the Price Structure page (Stocks tab).

Terms used, from Smart Money Concepts, each with an i button: order block, break of structure (BoS), change of character (CHoCH), swing high, swing low. Sweeps and plain breaks are worked out but not shown (11 Nov).

What is shown:
- Swing points as small dots, the last swing high and low as dotted lines.
- Markers for events, each with one sentence of what price did, for example "Closed above its last swing high while making higher highs and higher lows (Rs 1,240 from 4 Nov)" or "Dipped below its last swing low (Rs 1,168) and closed back above it".
- Order blocks as shaded bands labelled "Order block · date", described as "the last candle that moved the other way before the break". Darker if price has not come back to it, lighter once revisited, removed after a close through it.
- REMOVED 11 Nov (not shown on the site): under every event, the result of our own test: "Over the next 20 sessions, stocks did about the same as other stocks their size (+0.1 pts on average)", or "did on average 0.6 pts better/worse than other stocks their size", plus a warning when the result was not steady across the period.
- Daily counts across F&O stocks or all stocks, for example "Break of structure, up: 14". Not ranked.

What is never shown: entry, stop-loss, target, risk to reward, "bullish" or "bearish", "institutions", "smart money is buying", or any ranking of setups.

Footer on the page: "Order blocks, breaks of structure, changes of character and sweeps come from Smart Money Concepts. They describe chart shapes, not who traded. Nothing here is a recommendation, an entry, a stop or a target."

Instead every card ends with: "Order blocks, breaks of structure and changes of character describe chart shapes on daily candles, updated after the close. They are not predictions and not a recommendation." Our backtest results are kept internally (data/structure_stats.json). Question for compliance, only if we want them back: may we publish our own backtest results as past-performance wording?

Trend reading (added 11 Nov): one box at the top of the Price structure card, combining swing points with chart strength.
- Labels: Uptrend, Uptrend not yet confirmed, Turning up chart still weak, Downtrend, Downtrend not yet confirmed, Pullback in a strong chart, Sideways, Sideways in a strong chart, Sideways in a weak chart.
- "How" sentence, for example: "Swing points have turned down since 26 Oct, but chart strength 70 (Constructive) says the longer picture is still up. A dip inside an uptrend, or the start of a turn."
- "Where" sentence, for example: "Price Rs 811 is above its last swing high of Rs 735 (by 10.4%) and 21.2% above its last swing low of Rs 669. It is inside an order block band, Rs 808.50 to Rs 844.50."
- No forecast, no level to act on. Question for compliance: is "A dip inside an uptrend, or the start of a turn" acceptable, since it names two possibilities without choosing one?

## Trader-first wording (11 Nov 2026)
- Stock page Trend tile: one label from the trend reading list above, with its "How" sentence under it.
- Key levels card: "Key levels · nearest above and below today's price · not entries, stops or targets". Rows: Option ceiling (most call open interest), Option floor (most put open interest), Last swing high, Last swing low, Order block above/below, 52 week high/low, each with its distance from today's price.
- Money Flow headline example: "Foreign investors have turned buyers: bought Rs 50,058 cr net in the last 5 sessions, after net selling Rs 21,165 cr over 30."
- Compare: "A tie on the numbers: RELIANCE leads on latest quarter, ICICIBANK on price trend." (was "The choice depends on which of those matters to you").
- Market Pulse: "Smaller stocks led ... Buying reached smaller stocks, though traders also paid more for protection."

## Update, 20 Nov 2026: what changed, and what needs sign-off

### Already changed (the earlier sections above describe some old wording)
- **Stocks in focus** (section 2) is now **"Stocks in the news today"**: "results, big moves and unusual activity, not a view on what comes next". The "Signals up / Signals down / Mixed" tags and their colours are removed from the page, because live they were right 51% of the time. The track record still logs and checks the direction openly.
- **Chart strength bands** (section 5) now read as the trend so far: Strong uptrend, Uptrend, No clear trend, Downtrend, Strong downtrend. "Sideways in a strong chart" became "Sideways in a longer uptrend".
- **Option floor and ceiling:** no longer "writers defend these levels", "boxed between" or "capped". Our test (about 100,000 stock expiries) found prices crossed them slightly more often than other strikes; pages say where positions sit and quote the test.
- **Max pain:** pages quote our test: price moved toward it 47% of the time, less than a coin toss.
- **"AI mode"** is renamed **"Live ticker"**. No AI model is used on the site, so the old name claimed something that is not there.
- **Price Structure "tested" lines** now compare each event with stocks without the event; all show no meaningful edge.

### New, needs sign-off
1. **Strategy Builder** (F&O): members build their own index option strategy and see how it would have done since 2019. Labelled at the top: "Your strategy, not research. ... Results are simulated, end of day only, and say nothing about the future. This is not advice from 72 Street." Ready-made shapes are labelled "Common shapes to start from, not suggestions." Results under 30 trades are not shown. Question: is a simulated profit figure on a user-built strategy acceptable with this labelling?
2. **Index Mood** (F&O): India VIX mood (Calm / Normal / Nervous), the move options price by expiry and how often that range held since 2019, and a Cheap / Fair / Expensive option price label with the note that the label has not changed the odds. No stock is named.
3. **Telegram alerts:** messages restate what happened to a stock the member chose (crossed a price they set, results out, moved more than their level) and end with "What the data shows, not a recommendation to buy or sell."
4. **GIFT Nifty** on Today's pre-open line: a price and its change, no interpretation.

### Item 43: coloured chips beside the price on every stock page
The row under the company name shows chips such as **Uptrend**, **Cheaper than peers**, **Profit +34% YoY** in green and **Below peers**, **High debt** in red, next to the share price.
Risk: green and red beside a price can read as a buy or sell view, even though each chip is a fact.
- **Option A:** keep the colours (they summarise the facts quickly).
- **Option B (recommended):** neutral colour for judgement words (Uptrend, Cheaper than peers, Below peers); keep green and red only for plain numbers (returns, profit growth).
Please choose A or B; the change is about an hour of work.

### Licensing (fix list 42 and 60)
The site credits NSE's website, Yahoo Finance and Screener. A licensed feed is needed before the site scales. Table downloads (screener, results) are held back until then, because a bulk download is closer to redistribution than showing the data.
